name: Lambda Aurigae
description: A naked-eye star 12.6 parsecs away, 1.3 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.981 +/- 0.015 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.331 +/- 0.021

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.041 +/- 0.015

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5749 +/- 48

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 79.18 +/- 0.28 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 13 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.3 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.981 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.331 solar radii and 5,749 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 34411: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
